entries.proposition: Design: hospital-based case-control, convenience sampling, 50 first-febrile-seizure cases against 100 febrile controls, 24 months.
entries.snippet: Patients were enrolled as they were admitted, employing a convenience sampling strategy. After obtaining approval from the Institutional Ethics Committee and parental consent, 150 patients were enrolled.

experimental_context.system: children 6-60 months at one Indian tertiary hospital, case-control: first febrile seizure (n = 50) versus febrile illness without seizure (n = 100)
experimental_context.endpoint: blood count and iron indices at admission

entries.proposition: Exclusions: children receiving iron therapy, developmental delay, or prior febrile seizure.
entries.snippet: Children receiving iron therapy, those with developmental delays, and those with a history of febrile seizures were excluded.

entries.proposition: Analysis: unpaired t-tests and chi-square only; no adjustment for age, weight, temperature or infection.
entries.snippet: Quantitative data were represented using mean and standard deviation, and normality was tested using the Shapiro-Wilk test.

entries.proposition: Anaemia (haemoglobin below 11) was present in 96 percent of cases and 85 percent of controls (p = 0.045); the control group of febrile children was itself anaemic in the great majority.
entries.snippet: In this study, we observed that 48 (96%) of cases and 85 (85%) of controls were anaemic (Hb < 11 g/dL), which was statistically significantly different (p=0.045).

entries.proposition: The Discussion gives the control anaemia rate as 86 percent (Results and Table 3 say 85) and reports a fourfold odds without an interval.
entries.snippet: Anaemia was observed in 96% of cases and 86% of controls in this study, with the likelihood of a febrile seizure being four times higher in anaemic patients than in non-anaemic patients.

entries.proposition: Authors' conclusion: iron deficiency anaemia is called a correctable risk factor, and screening and supplementation after a first seizure are advised.
entries.snippet: Screening for iron deficiency anaemia should be prioritised for children experiencing their first seizure episode, as early diagnosis and timely iron supplementation may help mitigate the risk.
